scores.comment: The voice is genuinely distinctive — declarative, restrained, poet-like. 'It is the 6am light through a steel kettle' is strong. However, it occasionally slides into precious territory: 'liturgical', 'monozukuri' feel performatively intellectual. The voice is consistent but risks sounding like every premium-craft brand that discovered Kinfolk in 2015. No egregious buzzwords detected, which earns points. But it lacks Fellow's actual wit — the brand's own copy ('romantic candlelit dinner') signals self-aware humor that is entirely absent here.

ICP is competent but generic: 'Urban specialty coffee enthusiasts, design-forward professionals aged 28–45.' This describes the customer of La Marzocco, Onyx Coffee, and Blue Bottle equally. Fellow's actual ICP skews toward the obsessive home barista who reads Barista Hustle, watches James Hoffmann at 2x speed, and tracks EY1 extraction yields. The 'meditative act' framing is soft — Fellow's real buyers are precision-obsessed, not zen-seekers. The brief romanticizes the ritual at the expense of the technical credibility that Fellow's audience actually demands.

Mostly strong. 'Origin is not a marketing word. It is the address of a flavor you will never forget.' — excellent. 'The farms remember. So do we.' — memorable. 'A kettle should feel inevitable in your hand.' — good. However: 'redefining what specialty coffee can be' is a tired trope. 'Four days of fermentation. A lifetime of terroir.' leans cliché. 'Nothing missing. Nothing superfluous.' is too close to generic luxury copy. The sourcing-ethos section name-drops actual products (Lucia's Guatemala, Rwanda Nyampinga) which is strong, specific, correct. Overall above average but not Pentagram-tier.

Palette is internally coherent: near-black background (#0F0E0C), warm cream foreground (#F2EDE6), muted gold accent (#C8A96E) — this reads like honest industrial warmth. The accent gold risks feeling like every other 'premium coffee' brand (Nespresso Vertuo range does this). The imagery treatment — 'high-contrast monochromatic base with warm sepia toning, 18% grain overlay, raking light' — is specific and consistent. Minor concern: the palette has no tension, no surprise. Everything reads as expected for the mood. A Sagmeister brief would introduce one dissonant element. This is safe coherence, not bold coherence.

These are genuinely above average for AI-generated briefs. The Ethiopia Anasora prompt ('bird's eye slow drift over drying cherries, rotates imperceptibly clockwise') is cinematic and specific. The tea cake prompt ('wooden pick separates fragment, fine dust rises, camera completely static') shows restraint and intent. The Series 1 prompt is solid. However: the Colombia El Diviso prompt ('deep amber coffee slowly fills') is competent but generic — could describe any pour-over video on YouTube. The Blackberry Co-Ferment prompt (blackberry sits among beans) is slightly on-the-nose/literal. Engine assignments (runway, kling, veo, hailuo, higgsfield) show knowledge but zero justification for why each engine per prompt.

The declared arc (ritual → ingredients → system) is logical but front-loaded with concept. In practice: manifesto → drops → espresso-system → sourcing-ethos → beyond-coffee. The sourcing-ethos section AFTER the espresso-system section breaks the arc — you've already sold the machine before explaining why the ingredients matter. The 'beyond-coffee' section feels tacked on rather than earned. The arc reads as a content-strategist structure, not a filmmaker's structure. There is no emotional low point, no turn. It escalates pleasantly but never surprises. The narrative is a straight line when it should breathe and curve.

The manifesto and drops sections have 3 body paragraphs each — appropriate for cinematic-narrative template. However, the espresso-system and sourcing-ethos sections also carry 3 paragraphs, creating a monotonous rhythm. The 'beyond-coffee' section is correctly shorter (2 paragraphs). A cinematic brief at this level should vary section density more aggressively — some sections should be single sentences, others longer meditations. Every section currently breathes at the same pace, which undermines the 'silence and white space carry weight' voice principle stated in the brief itself.

'cinematic-narrative' template is a correct choice for Fellow's premium-industrial, object-worship aesthetic. The film-grain signature reinforces it. The slow-reveal, object-forward visual language described in the imagery treatment aligns with what this template should deliver. No mismatch. Minor concern: Fellow also sells a significant volume of specialty coffee drops (12+ SKUs in catalog) — a cinematic-narrative template may undersell the editorial velocity of the drops program. A hybrid editorial-cinematic might serve better. But given the brief's intent, the choice is defensible.

'film-grain' signature is contextually correct — it reinforces analog warmth, human craft, the anti-digital-sterility positioning. It aligns with the Kinfolk/monozukuri reference. However, film grain as a visual signature has become extremely common in craft/specialty coffee branding (See Also Coffee, La Cabra, etc.). It is correct but not distinctive. A more unexpected signature — say 'blueprint technical' or 'single-source light study' — would have set Fellow apart rather than placing it in a familiar visual dialect. Points for correctness, deducted for lack of courage.

'The ritual begins before the first sip.' — 8 words exactly (at the limit), declarative, clean. However, it is not MEMORABLE. It describes an idea without owning it. Replace 'ritual' and 'sip' with synonyms and the sentence could be written for Aesop, Mate, or any wellness brand. It has no Fellow-specific DNA. Compare to what a premium agency might produce: 'The kettle is also the argument.' or 'Wrong tools. Wrong cup. Right obsession.' The brief's own copy is stronger in the body than in the hero. The subheadline ('Precision instruments and single-origin coffees for those who understand...') is too long and explanatory — a confession that the headline isn't strong enough to stand alone.

priorities.what: Réécrire le hero headline pour qu'il soit spécifiquement Fellow — pas interchangeable avec n'importe quelle marque craft premium
priorities.why: 'The ritual begins before the first sip.' est générique. Il ne contient aucun ADN Fellow : ni la précision obsessionnelle, ni l'humour sec, ni la tension design/café. C'est le headline que 40 marques de specialty coffee ont déjà. Le subheadline compense — ce qui est un aveu d'échec du headline.
priorities.how: Travailler sur l'axe tension design/obsession plutôt que rituel/spiritualité. Exemples de direction : 'Built for the 6am argument with yourself.' / 'The kettle is also the discipline.' / 'Wrong variable. Wrong cup. Start over.' — quelque chose qui capture l'obsession du home barista Fellow, pas le zen générique. Tester < 7 mots. Interdire les mots : ritual, sip, morning, craft, perfect.

priorities.what: Reconstruire la narrative arc pour qu'elle ait une vraie tension dramatique — pas un flux de montée en gamme linéaire
priorities.why: L'arc actuel (manifeste → drops → machine → sourcing → tea) est une liste éditoriale, pas une structure narrative. La sourcing-ethos APRÈS la machine casse la logique causale. Il n'y a aucun moment de retournement, de tension, de doute. Une agence Pentagram construirait une vraie tension : la promesse → la réalité brute du terroir → la machine comme réponse → la preuve → l'invitation.
priorities.how: Réordonner : 1) Manifeste (la question inconfortable), 2) Sourcing-ethos (d'où vient le café — ancrer dans le réel avant de vendre la machine), 3) Drops (preuves concrètes du goût), 4) Espresso System (la machine comme réponse à ce que tu viens de goûter), 5) Beyond-Coffee (expansion earned). Ajouter une section courte — une seule ligne — entre sourcing et machine, qui joue le rôle de 'pont' dramatique.

priorities.what: Injecter la voix réelle de Fellow dans le brief — l'humour sec, l'auto-conscience de marque, disparaissent entièrement
priorities.why: Le scrape original dit : 'What happens when a love for coffee and a passion for product design meet up for a romantic candlelit dinner? Fellow happens.' C'est une marque qui a de l'esprit, de l'ironie, une légèreté précise. Le brief actuel transforme Fellow en marque solennelle et liturgique à la Aesop — ce qui est un contresens de positionnement. Le résultat sonne plus 'premium Japanese craft brand' que 'opinionated SF design company'.
priorities.how: Introduire 1-2 touches d'humour sec dans la voix : une note de bas de manifeste qui casse la solennité, une caption produit qui assume l'obsession avec autodérision ('Yes, it's 1745€. No, you won't regret it.'). Retravailler le footer tagline — 'For the cup that earns the morning' est trop noble. Quelque chose comme : 'Fellow. Because the wrong kettle is a problem that compounds daily.' — garde la précision mais retrouve la personnalité.

summary: Ce brief est au-dessus de la moyenne des outputs IA — le copy a de vrais moments, les video prompts sont spécifiques, la palette est cohérente. Mais il commet le péché capital du branding IA premium : il efface la personnalité distinctive de la marque source pour la remplacer par une esthétique 'specialty craft générique' que n'importe quelle agence mid-tier produirait pour n'importe quel client café. Fellow n'est pas La Cabra. Fellow n'est pas See Also Coffee. Fellow est une marque SF avec de l'humour, de l'obsession technique, et un positionnement design-first qui a une voix propre — tout ça disparaît au profit d'un template Kinfolk-monozukuri solide mais interchangeable. Le hero headline est le symptôme le plus visible : 8 mots corrects, 0 mémorabilité Fellow-spécifique. Le brief mérite d'être repassé en amélioration ciblée, pas régénéré entièrement — la structure technique est saine, c'est la voix et la tension narrative qui manquent.
